questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Eating insects and changing people's attitudes
How to cook traditional Italian pasta at home
Why insects are dangerous pests on farms
The best fusion restaurants around the world
questions.why: Neil says they're discussing food made from bugs, and experts explain how to change attitudes to it.

questions.q: How does Sam feel about eating food made from bugs at first?
options: She has eaten it many times and loves it
She wants to try a tarantula doughnut
She doesn't like the idea
She thinks it's healthier than meat
questions.why: Sam says 'Maybe not' – the idea of eating bugs and creepy crawlies 'doesn't appeal'.

questions.q: What benefits of eating insects does Neil mention?
options: They are cheaper than any other kind of food
They're nutritious and could fight hunger
They taste better than meat and fish
They help people lose weight quickly
questions.why: He says they're full of nutrients like protein and could help fight world hunger and reduce pollution.

questions.q: According to Andy Holcroft, why is it hard to get Western people to eat insects?
options: Insects are too expensive in Western shops
It's against the law in many Western countries
There aren't enough insect farms yet
People think they'll taste awful before trying
questions.why: He says 'we already think before we've even tried them, they're going to taste disgusting or gross'.

questions.q: What does Andy find is the easiest way to get people to try insects?
options: Cookies made with cricket powder
Whole spiders cooked in oil
Insect tapas served with wine
Worms mixed into pasta dishes
questions.why: He suggests a chocolate-chip cricket cookie made with cricket powder, so you don't see any insects.

questions.q: How does chef Joseph Yoon react when people say 'urghh' about insects?
options: He argues with them until they agree
He tells them they are being silly
He is understanding and doesn't argue
He stops talking to them about food
questions.why: He says, 'I don't get confrontational… I understand that you can feel that way.'

questions.q: How does Joseph want people to think of insects?
options: As pests that bite and carry disease
As a cheap food only for poor countries
As animals that should be protected
As food farmed sustainably for people
questions.why: He wants to change perceptions from pests to edible insects, 'sustainably farmed… for human consumption'.

questions.q: Why does Neil mention cows and sheep near the end?
options: To say that meat is better for you than insects
To suggest eating insects is no different
To explain how insects are farmed
To show that farming animals is bad for the planet
questions.why: He says we kill animals such as cows and sheep to eat, 'so why not insects or spiders?'
